chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from al-'Umariyyi, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a woman who gave birth from adultery (zina), is it permissible for her milk to be used for wet-nursing? He said: No, it is not permissible, nor is the milk of her daughter who was born from adultery.

key_terms.لَا يَصۡلُحُ: It is not permissible / not suitable

ai.seo_question: Is the milk of a woman who gave birth from zina permissible for wet-nursing?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam Ali ibn Ja'far (or his brother Abu al-Hasan al-Kazim) establishes that the milk of a woman who gave birth from illicit sexual relations (*zina*) is not suitable for wet-nursing, extending this impurity or distinct status to her daughter born from the same act. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic view on the transmission of physical or spiritual characteristics through lineage and milk, emphasizing the purity required for nursing. The extension to the daughter underscores the continuity of this specific legal status within the maternal line affected by *zina*.
